=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (multiple images show leaves emerging in distinct pairs from the same node along the stem)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are densely packed at the terminal shoot tips)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade attached to the stem)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf edges are smooth, though some minor mechanical damage is present)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaves are broadly oval with the widest point near the middle)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute to acuminate (leaf tips taper to a distinct, sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf bases taper gradually into the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a single central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching from it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible and prominent, curving towards the leaf margin (arcuate)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaves reflect light, indicating a glabrous and somewhat glossy surface)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are relatively short compared to the leaf blade size)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the visible stem appears thin, green, and non-woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: green (the stem is green, similar to the leaf color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels are visible)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no distinct jointed swelling is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling displays a distinct terminal cluster of leaves. Some leaves show minor physical damage such as small holes and notches on the margins. A pink tag is visible near the base, likely for identification purposes.
